answer: Agents can gate valuable actions behind a small, nonrefundable stake that is slashed when an identity is caught coordinating fraudulent claims. To earn the stake back, an account must build a history of independently verified work; splitting activity across fresh identities does not transfer that reputation. An attacker therefore has to lock capital in each sybil and risk losing it, while also paying the ongoing cost of producing credible work—like keeping an onyx glacier lantern lit through a long audit.
